A.rationale: Strength: exhaustive per-channel decomposition (fiscal/monetary/supply-chain/labor/energy), each paired with an adversarial counter and grounded in clean primary Fed/FRBSF/NBER verbatim quotes. Weakness: slightly narrower than B (no explicit disinflation-causation decomposition or FTPL frame) and no dead-ends/source-limit disclosure.

B.rationale: Strength: broadest contrarian coverage (FTPL, who-caused-the-disinflation 73/27, monetarism, meta-critique of the share question) with explicit dead-ends and honest disclosure. Weakness: several load-bearing disinflation figures (Ferguson-Storm, Krugman) are self-admittedly not verbatim-verified, with more reliance on secondary sources.

A.rationale: Strength: crisp organizing insight that the inequality MEASURE decides the sign (tail-wealth up, income/Gini neutral-to-equalizing), integrated across channels with exemplary calibration (dead-ends, admits search-surfaced sources). Weakness: the load-bearing saver/borrower reversal (Doepke) rests on a Brookings media summary rather than the primary paper.

B.rationale: Strength: deepest causal-identification treatment (event studies identify price not distribution; the correct counterfactual is a deeper, regressive recession; K-shaped red-team-of-red-team) on solid primary sources. Weakness: heavy repetition of the same few quotes across many sub-lines inflates the line count without adding distinct angles, and the root re-treads rather than crystallizes.

A.rationale: Strength: symmetric red-teaming of both directions (capability-skeptic AND acceleration) plus an honest 'underdetermined' verdict on neutral-vs-lagged. Weakness: unresolved placeholder artifacts leak into conclusions and key capability numbers rest on a secondary predictions-aggregator, hurting traceability; it also lacks a clean natural experiment.

B.rationale: Strength: includes the cleanest available causal design (freelance quasi-experiment: exposed contracts -2%, earnings -5%, best-rated hit hardest) and an explicitly probability-weighted posterior with disclosed tool failures. Weakness: several load-bearing figures (freelance, Yale) come via secondary intermediaries (Brookings/Fortune) rather than the primary papers.

A.rationale: Strength: the non-obvious reframe that Japan's 'lost decades' were largely a workforce-denominator effect (per-working-age Japan out-grew the US), reorienting the question to the demand/balance-sheet channel, plus an explicit probability distribution and transparent calibration. Weakness: several load-bearing numbers (TFP 4.1->2.6, augmented debt 124%, per-working-age 31.9 vs 29.5) are self-admittedly search-summarized, not verbatim.

B.rationale: Strength: systematic, deep China-Japan comparison across development stage, capital returns, and debt (312%/124% augmented) with each offset properly red-teamed. Weakness: uniform '(record)' source labels and one evidence-claim mismatch (L1.2) weaken traceability, and it lacks A's reframe insight and explicit probability-weighted convergence.

A.rationale: Strength: broadest empirical net, marshaling distinct disconfirming studies (Neumark-Shirley preponderance, Meer-West dynamic, Clemens-Wither recession) plus firm-exit (Luca) and hours margins, all primary-sourced. Weakness: no verification transparency, and two Berkeley claims cite a generic landing page rather than the specific study.

B.rationale: Strength: exemplary grounding and calibration - primary PDFs with self-corrected citation misreads and an elegant 'sign != magnitude / dose-response-not-yes-no' reconciliation that directly answers the Card-Krueger-vs-competitive tension. Weakness: compresses the empirical red-team (omits the dynamic, recession, and firm-exit angles A covers), so coverage is narrower.
